title: Rigidity of Symmetric-Gradient Differential Inclusions
statement: What structure can be proved for sufficiently regular $u$ satisfying the differential inclusion $Eu\in\{\lambda(a\mathbin{\odot}b):\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$?
background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Calculus of Variations (2013), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2012/36, pp. 2205--2268](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2012/36)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** BD structure theorems and good blow-up results give substantial one-directional rigidity for the symmetric-gradient inclusion, but they do not provide a complete classification in the generality asked.

**Sources checked.**

- [De Philippis--Rindler, structure of A-free measures](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.06543)
- [De Philippis--Rindler, symmetric-gradient Young measures](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04097)
- [De Philippis--Rindler, fine properties of BD](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01356)
